```{r setup, include=FALSE}
sizing <- read.csv("../output/opportunity_sizing.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sens <- read.csv("../output/sensitivity.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
q2 <- read.csv("../output/q2_worst_step_test.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

v <- function(item) sizing$value[sizing$item == item]
fmt_usd <- function(x) scales::dollar(x)
fmt_pct <- function(x) scales::percent(x, accuracy = 0.1)
fmt_n <- function(x) scales::comma(x, accuracy = 1)

lift <- v("relative_lift")
be_lift <- v("break_even_lift")
net <- v("net_benefit_year1")
roi <- v("roi_year1")
payback <- v("payback_months")
gp <- v("incremental_gross_profit_year")
rev <- v("incremental_revenue_year")
purch <- v("incremental_purchases_year")
addr <- v("addressable_sessions_year")
build <- v("build_cost_usd")
maint <- v("yearly_maintenance_usd")
base_conv <- v("baseline_step_conversion")
ctp <- v("cart_to_purchase_conversion")
aov_usd <- v("aov_usd")
dropped <- q2$dropped_sessions[1]
lift_swing <- sens$swing[1] / 1e3
build_swing <- sens$swing[sens$input == "build_cost_usd"] / 1e3

tbl <- data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "View→cart step conversion today",
    "Sessions lost at the step (92 days)",
    "Addressable sessions per year",
    "Cart→purchase conversion",
    "Assumed relative lift on the step",
    "Average order value (pre-holiday)",
    "Incremental purchases per year",
    "Incremental revenue per year",
    "Incremental gross profit per year",
    "Build cost (one-time)",
    "Yearly maintenance",
    "Net benefit, year 1",
    "ROI, year 1",
    "Payback",
    "Break-even lift"
  ),
  Value = c(
    fmt_pct(base_conv),
    fmt_n(dropped),
    fmt_n(addr),
    fmt_pct(ctp),
    fmt_pct(lift),
    fmt_usd(aov_usd),
    fmt_n(purch),
    fmt_usd(rev),
    fmt_usd(gp),
    fmt_usd(build),
    fmt_usd(maint),
    fmt_usd(net),
    fmt_pct(roi),
    paste0(round(payback, 1), " months"),
    fmt_pct(be_lift)
  )
)
```

# Recommendation

**Don't build it yet.** At the assumed `r fmt_pct(lift)` lift, fixing the view→cart step earns only `r fmt_usd(net)` in year one — barely above break-even (the minimum lift that pays for itself is `r fmt_pct(be_lift)`). Run a cheap A/B experiment to prove the lift first; build only if it clears `r fmt_pct(be_lift)`.

# Why

- **The step is the biggest leak:** view→cart drops `r fmt_n(dropped)` sessions in 92 days — the single largest absolute funnel loss, at a `r fmt_pct(base_conv)` conversion.
- **But the prize is small:** even a `r fmt_pct(lift)` lift yields only `r fmt_n(purch)` incremental purchases (~`r fmt_usd(rev)` revenue, `r fmt_usd(gp)` gross profit) per year against a `r fmt_usd(build)` build plus `r fmt_usd(maint)`/year upkeep.
- **The answer hinges on one assumption:** the assumed lift swings year-1 net benefit by ~`r fmt_n(lift_swing)`k USD in sensitivity, while build cost swings it by only `r fmt_n(build_swing)`k — so an experiment that measures the lift is the highest-value next step.

# Cost and return

```{r}
knitr::kable(tbl)
```

The project breaks even at a `r fmt_pct(be_lift)` lift on the step. Below that, net benefit is negative.

![Sensitivity tornado](../charts/sizing_tornado.png)

# What would change my mind

- A **measured lift** (from an A/B test) at or above `r fmt_pct(be_lift)` — that converts this from a bet on an assumption into a positive-ROI build.
- Evidence that the **cart→purchase downstream** (`r fmt_pct(ctp)` today) improves with a better cart experience, multiplying the value of the fix.
- The **device parity result changing**: the funnel is uniform across devices now; a device-specific cliff would change the target and the sizing.
- A **bigger lift upside** — if the assumed high case (`r fmt_pct(sens$high_value[1])`) is credible, the swing analysis shows the payoff re-rates the whole decision.

# Method + limitations

- **Observational data:** the GA4 public sample is one ecommerce store over 92 days; effects are correlations, not causal evidence. All figures come from `output/` CSVs and the committed snapshot.
- **Obfuscated sample:** Google replaces some values with placeholders (e.g. `<Other>`); zero-revenue purchases are obfuscated NULLs and were excluded from AOV, not dropped silently.
- **Holiday window:** Black Friday through Christmas sits inside the sample; sizing uses the pre-holiday AOV as business-as-usual and annualizes the 92-day funnel.
- **Assumed lift:** the `r fmt_pct(lift)` point lift is an assumption, not a measured effect; the tornado chart and break-even lift make that explicit.
